Wanted to share my experience so far to balance out all the negative reviews. I'm sure those people are legitimately having issues, but those issues do not affect everyone.

Red Dead Redemption 2 was already practically my favorite game after playing it on PS4 and being blown away by the story, gameplay, and amazing environment in which it takes place. Leading up to the release on Steam I was little worried after hearing about some of the issues with the PC launch, but I'm very happy that I have had zero issues with the game now that my wife bought it for me as an early Christmas gift. No launcher issues, no crashing, and it runs beautifully.

FRAME RATE TIP: Turning down graphics settings related to water makes a huge difference. I was only getting about 35 FPS near the river in the first area of the game. I turned water physics down to the second highest notch and gained 20+ frames per second. Now about 5 hours in and the frame rate has remained at a smooth 55-60 FPS at minimum (quite a bit more in some scenes), with everything set to ultra aside from turning water physics down one notch.

As long as you're not one of the unfortunate souls with launcher issues and crashing, you're in for one of the most amazing video game experiences of this generation.

Red Dead Redemption 2 Review - 96 Hours In 

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

96 hours into Red Dead Redemption 2 , and I’m completely immersed in one of the most breathtaking gaming experiences ever created. Rockstar truly outdid themselves with this masterpiece, crafting a game where every moment feels cinematic and impactful.

Highlights 
✔️ Stunning Open World: From sweeping vistas to bustling towns, every corner of the map feels alive and meticulously detailed.
✔️ Compelling Storyline: Arthur Morgan’s journey is emotional, gripping, and filled with moral complexity.
✔️ Endless Activities: Hunting, fishing, poker, robberies, or simply riding through the wilderness—there’s always something to do.
✔️ Realistic Mechanics: The attention to detail, like horse care and weapon maintenance, adds depth to the experience.
✔️ Dynamic NPCs: Characters react to you in unique and often surprising ways, enhancing immersion.

Cons 
❌ Slower Pacing: Not everyone will appreciate the deliberate pace of exploration and storytelling.
❌ Controls Can Be Clunky: Some mechanics, like aiming or horse movement, can feel awkward at times.

Final Thoughts 
Red Dead Redemption 2 is nothing short of a masterpiece. The world Rockstar created feels real, and the story stays with you long after the game ends. Whether you’re a fan of action, exploration, or narrative-driven games, this title is a must-play. I’m not even close to being done and can’t wait to see what else this epic adventure holds.

If you found this review helpful, please give it a like or an award! Thanks for reading, and happy trails!

Red Dead Redemption 2 is a western themed open world singleplayer+multiplayer action game. This game is one of the best singleplayer games I've ever played, however I didn't like the multiplayer version that much. Here is my pro-con list about the game:

Pros:

-Exceptional story
-Outstanding visuals
-Great soundtrack
-The best character development I've ever seen in a game/film/TV show
-Riding a horse is satisfying
-Great physics
-Interactions with the NPCs are highly effective in the game
-Towns and cities are greatly decorated
-Choices really matter, both affects the game and the player
-Board games are fun
-Plot twists <3
-You can talk with your horse
-Atmosphere is perfect
-Weapons and customization
-Optimization is great
-Game is well executed
-Play time is long enough
-You're alright my boah

Cons

-There is no vocalization in multiplayer
-Game is a bit slowly paced at the beginning, so it might lose players who aren't patient enough
-You cannot go back to the older save file after you die, it randomizes the place, and you cannot get your old horse if your horse is dead. This can be counted as a good realistic feature, but I lost legendary bear fur, so I didn't like it.

Overall: This game is a greatly executed game with a perfect story, physics, sound, visuals, atmosphere, gameplay, and choices. I would give 9.8/10 for single player and 5.4/10 for multiplayer

Mesmerizing Storytelling:
The narrative is considered epic and reminiscent of the best westerns, with a focus on compelling characters like Arthur Morgan.

Emotional Impact:
The game's story and character development create a deeply immersive experience, making players feel connected to the characters and their struggles.

Slow Burn:
The game's deliberate pace allows for a richer exploration of the characters and their relationships, building a strong bond with both the main characters and the game's world.

Lifelike Open World:
The game's open world is praised for its realism and stunning detail, with a diverse range of environments, from bustling towns to serene landscapes.

Immersive Experience:
The game's attention to detail, including the vastness of the world, the wildlife, and the interactions with NPCs, creates a truly immersive experience.

No Time Wasted:
Every action in the game feels meaningful and contributes to the overall narrative and experience.

Rockstar has always been great at making funny and huge open world games, and I think this one is my favorite of theirs and one of my favorite games overall. The characters super memorable and the story is such a blast, yet with that being said, be warned because there are some things about the game that are super annoying and could be easily fixed yet aren't. You have to launch the game through their rockstar launcher which you HAVE to be online to go through or else it won't let you play, then you have to go to sound mixer and change the volume from 8 (which it's set to every time you start the game) back up to 100. Also, the saving for rockstar games is a lot more annoying than other open world games like skyrim or the witcher, you can't save during missions and there's no quicksave, you have to manually save every time which takes like 30 seconds longer, also with only like 10 save slots. To be fair you can replay any mission you've completed at any time but still, I'd rather just have the more mainstream way of saving. All in all, I think the game makes up for that, especially being so long of a game yet filled with unique missions.

A real living breathing world. One of if not the most immersive game worlds ever created, though it is a very slow game because its almost like being there in the old west for real. Some may like that, others may love the immersion.

It has some of the most realistic NPCs with actual AI that works, which seems rare for games of today. You can even talk to every NPC and there is a lot of interaction.

It also has, while small considering its the old west, the most immersive towns and "cities" (for the time period) ever created in a game. The towns are amazing, and never have I seen such amazing detail with so much interaction, realism and actual npcs that look like they belong there in towns/cities that know how to move out of your way than I have this game.

Definitely highly recommended if you are looking for a highly immersive, slow paced game, where you can actually feel like you are really living in the old west.
